game_config._comment_belt_items_per_tile: Items one belt tile holds (1-4). Belt throughput = belt speed (tiles/s, 1 base, raised by ConveyorSpeed research) x this.
game_config._comment_purchase_scaling: Each successive placement of the same building type costs more. Formula: base_cost × multiplier^(n-1) where n = number of buildings of that type already placed.

pve._comment: PvE tournaments (docs/agents/tasks/feature-pve-tournaments.md). Shared by the client (GameConfigSO.pve) and the PvE Cloud Code module, which embeds this file: REDEPLOY the module after changing it. Leagues run bottom to top; promote/demote scale down for brackets below bracket_size. Reward bands are tried in order: rank_to (rank <= n), else top_percent, else everyone. First-pass reward values 2026-11-23, revisit in phase 5.

game_config._comment_name_filter_patterns: Public player names (tournament leaderboards) may not match any of these regexes (PlayerNameRules; the PvE server re-checks). Each is tried on the lower-cased name AND its normalised form: leetspeak mapped (0 o, 1 i, 3 e, 4 a, 5 s, 7 t, @ a, $ s), _ and - dropped, repeated letters collapsed. So write letters with + (b+a+d) and anchor short roots (^...$) to avoid blocking ordinary words.

research.description: Harness the strong nuclear force to bind quarks into protons and neutrons — and combine them with electrons to form the first atoms.
research.codex_entry: The foundational discovery enabling nucleon synthesis. By controlling the strong force, quarks can be permanently bound into stable protons and neutrons.

research.description: Combine a proton and an electron to form the simplest atom: hydrogen.
research.codex_entry: The simplest atom: one proton orbited by one electron. Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe and the gateway to all atomic chemistry.

research.description: Unlocks the Harvester — a field collector that gathers particles continuously without manual input. Also unlocks the Filter for sorting belts. Hold a belt to split it.
research.codex_entry: Continuous field collection without manual input. A Harvester placed on a quantum field extracts particles automatically at its rated output rate.

research._comment: Lets the player buy and place extra fields from the Build menu. Prices live on each field (purchase_cost_*), so this node gates no building.
research.description: Condense new quark and lepton fields onto empty tiles. Quark fields come in pairs. Each one costs ten times the last.
research.codex_entry: A field is only a region where the vacuum is unusually generous. Pump enough entropy into empty space and it learns to give up particles too, though every new field strains the vacuum more than the last.

research.description: Teach the Atom Generator to build Helium-4 from 2 protons, 2 neutrons and 2 electrons. Heavier atoms need fusion.
research.codex_entry: Combining protons, neutrons, and electrons into stable atoms. Each element's identity is defined by its proton count — change it and you change the element.

research.description: Teach the Atom Generator to build Deuterium (1 proton, 1 neutron, 1 electron): heavy hydrogen, the fuel for your first fusion.
research.codex_entry: Deuterium is hydrogen with a neutron attached. One in every 6,400 hydrogen atoms in Earth's oceans is deuterium. Fusing two of them is far easier than fusing bare protons, which is why every fusion experiment on Earth starts with it.

research.description: Unlocks the Power Relay — a mast that broadcasts the grid's power over a wide radius without generating any eV, letting one generator feed distant buildings.
research.codex_entry: Power need not be generated where it is used. A resonant relay re-radiates the grid's existing eV field across a far wider area than any single generator can reach, decoupling where you make power from where you spend it.

research.description: Unlock the Nucleon Harvester: place one across two quark fields, or merge two neighbouring Harvesters (Up and Down Quarks) into one. Makes protons or neutrons with no Combiner.
research.codex_entry: Two harvesters on opposing polarity fields can be merged into a single Nucleon Harvester, producing protons or neutrons directly without quark combination.

items.codex_entry: One of two quark flavours that compose protons and neutrons. Carries a +2/3 electric charge. Quarks are permanently confined — they cannot exist freely outside a hadron.
The heavier of the two light quarks, carrying a -1/3 electric charge. Two down quarks and one up quark bind together to form a neutron.
A fundamental lepton with a -1 charge. Orbits the nucleus of atoms and determines all chemical bonding behaviour. No internal structure has ever been detected.
A baryon composed of two up quarks and one down quark, bound by the strong nuclear force. The number of protons in a nucleus defines which element it is — this number is the atomic number.
A baryon composed of one up quark and two down quarks. Electrically neutral. Adding or removing neutrons from a nucleus produces isotopes of the same element.
The simplest and most abundant element in the universe. One proton, one electron — the starting point for all atomic chemistry. The primary fuel of stars.
The second lightest element, produced in stellar cores through hydrogen fusion. A noble gas — chemically inert. Its nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons) is identical to an alpha particle.
A soft alkali metal and the lightest solid element. Critical in battery technology — the backbone of rechargeable batteries used in every mobile device.
The basis of all organic chemistry. Carbon's ability to form four bonds makes it the backbone of life. Also exists as graphite, diamond, and graphene.
The third most abundant element in the universe. Highly reactive and essential for combustion and respiration. Makes up 21% of Earth's atmosphere.
A semiconductor at the heart of modern electronics. Silicon wafers are the foundation of processors, solar cells, and transistors.
The most common element on Earth by mass. The endpoint of stellar fusion — stars cannot fuse elements heavier than iron without consuming more energy than they produce.

The heaviest naturally occurring element. Radioactive — decays slowly over billions of years. The primary fuel for nuclear fission reactors. Requires advanced assembly techniques. Decays: alpha decay turns it into Thorium (Decay Chamber).
A stable isotope of hydrogen with one added neutron. Found naturally in heavy water. An essential fuel for nuclear fusion reactions alongside tritium.
The fissile isotope of uranium used in nuclear reactors and weapons. Splitting U-235 releases enormous energy and produces alpha particles as decay byproducts.

Emitted during alpha decay of heavy radioactive isotopes. Equivalent to a helium-4 nucleus: 2 protons + 2 neutrons. Collected by Radioactive Containment buildings and used as a secondary energy currency.
Emitted during beta decay of unstable isotopes like Tritium and Carbon-14. A high-energy electron. Collected by Radioactive Containment buildings and fed back into the power grid.
Harder than steel and lighter than aluminium. Beryllium is transparent to X-rays and used in nuclear reactor reflectors. Toxic in dust form — handle with care.
A metalloid bridging metals and nonmetals. Boron carbide is one of the hardest materials known. Boron-10 absorbs neutrons, making it essential for nuclear reactor control rods.
78% of Earth's atmosphere. Nitrogen is the limiting nutrient in agriculture — the Haber process that synthesises ammonia from it feeds half of humanity.
The most abundant metal in Earth's crust, yet rare in pure form before electrolysis was discovered. Lightweight and corrosion-resistant — the backbone of aerospace and packaging.
A transition metal with strong magnetic properties. Critical in stainless steel, lithium-nickel battery cathodes, and superalloys that survive jet engine temperatures.
The best electrical conductor among common metals. In our Quantum Foundry, copper is synthesised atom by atom — ironic, given it is the cheapest ore in simpler mining games.
Zinc galvanises steel against corrosion and is half of brass alloy. Essential in human biology as a cofactor in hundreds of enzymes.
The highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any element. Used in solar panel contacts, antibacterial coatings, and high-performance circuit connections.
Chemically inert, immune to corrosion, and malleable beyond any other metal. Every connector in space hardware is gold-plated. Its rarity is a product of neutron star collisions.
The premier catalytic metal. Platinum in catalytic converters eliminates toxic exhaust. In fuel cells it enables hydrogen-oxygen reactions at room temperature. Rarer than gold.
The highest melting point of any element — 3,422°C. Rocket nozzles, light filaments, and plasma-facing components in fusion reactors all rely on tungsten's thermal extremity.
Does not occur naturally on Earth — only made in reactors and particle accelerators. Pu-239 is the most energy-dense fissile fuel known. Assembling it requires exquisite precision.
Two hydrogen, one oxygen — the universal solvent and prerequisite for life as we know it. In the Foundry it is a chemical intermediate and coolant feedstock.
Hydrogen as it is found: paired into H₂ molecules, the lightest gas there is. Chemistry's first feedstock.
Diatomic oxygen, the reactive fifth of the air. With hydrogen it burns to water.
Carbon as it is mined: sheets of hexagonal rings, soft enough to write with. The backbone of every organic molecule.
Four fifths of the air, held together by one of the strongest bonds in chemistry. Breaking it makes ammonia.
The simplest hydrocarbon. Natural gas is mostly methane. SpaceX's Raptor engine burns it with oxygen. A key carbon feedstock for synthesising carbon fibre and polymers.
The Haber–Bosch synthesis of ammonia is arguably the most important industrial reaction in history — it enabled fertilisers that now feed half the world's population.
Silicon dioxide — the primary component of sand, glass, and quartz. Ultrapure silica is the substrate from which semiconductor wafers are grown.
Iron oxide — rust — is the thermite reaction's fuel and the precursor ore for steel production. In the Foundry we synthesise it directly from pure iron and oxygen.
Iron alloyed with controlled carbon content. The structural material of the industrial age — bridges, skyscrapers, ships. Synthesised here by reducing iron oxide with methane.
Crystalline carbon arranged in long chains — five times stronger than steel at one quarter the weight. The structural material of spacecraft, racing vehicles, and megastructures.
Titanium alloyed with aluminium and vanadium — the aerospace standard. Survives re-entry temperatures, resists saltwater corrosion, and biocompatible enough for implants.
Ultrapure crystalline silicon sliced to sub-millimetre thickness. The substrate on which every integrated circuit is etched. Grown from molten silica in hydrogen atmosphere.
The lightest solid material ever synthesised — 99.8% air by volume. An extraordinary thermal insulator. Used in Mars rover heat shields and as structural fill in megastructures.
A material with zero electrical resistance below its critical temperature. Enables MRI machines, maglev trains, and the magnetic confinement coils of fusion reactors.
Engineered at the nanoscale to have properties impossible in natural materials — negative refractive index, electromagnetic cloaking, and exotic gravitational interactions.
A processor that harnesses quantum superposition and entanglement. Factorises problems in polynomial time that classical computers cannot solve in the lifetime of the universe.
A toroidal magnetic confinement structure that holds stellar plasma at 150 million degrees — hotter than the sun's core. The heart of a fusion power plant or a miniature star.
A magnetic bottle storing antihydrogen — matter's mirror. When antimatter meets matter, 100% of both masses convert to energy per E=mc². The most energy-dense storage known.
The structural anchor point of a Dyson sphere. Each node bears the gravitational tension of thousands of square kilometres of solar-collecting surface. Built to last a million years.
The load-bearing superstructure of a megastructure. Woven from titanium alloy and carbon fibre into a tensegrity lattice strong enough to encircle a star.
A metamaterial array that bends spacetime curvature. Compensates for tidal forces across the inner surface of a Dyson sphere, maintaining structural integrity against the star's gravity gradient.

items.codex_entry: One carbon bonded to two oxygens. The exhaust of combustion and the feedstock of photosynthesis.
The workhorse of industrial chemistry: a strong diprotic acid made from sulfur, oxygen, and hydrogen.
A powerful oxidizing acid of nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen. The reagent behind fertilizers, explosives, and etched metal.
The simplest two-carbon hydrocarbon. A short link in the chain that organic chemistry builds outward without end.
A hydrocarbon with an oxygen-hydrogen head — the first alcohol. Solvent, fuel, and a stepping stone to more complex organics.

items._bio_b1_note: Biology B1 biomolecules (Chem/Bio Biology track). Category Biomolecule. Assembled by the Biosynthesizer from organic compounds harvested on the Biology map. base_sell_value is FIRST-PASS (Phase 6 re-tier).
items.codex_entry: A folded chain of amino acids. Enzymes, motors, and scaffolds — proteins do nearly all the work of a living cell.
A polymer of sugars. The cell's fuel store and structural fiber, from starch to cellulose.
A bilayer of fatty acids that separates inside from outside. The first boundary — without it, there is no cell.
A chain of nucleotides — DNA and RNA. The molecule of heredity, storing and transcribing the instructions of life.

items._bio_b2_note: Biology B2 cellular components (Chem/Bio Biology track). Category CellPart. Assembled by the Cell Assembler. base_sell_value FIRST-PASS (Phase 6 re-tier).
items.codex_entry: The cell's factory floor: a complex of nucleic acid and protein that reads genetic code and builds new proteins.
The powerhouse of the cell. A membrane-bound organelle that burns fuel into usable energy.
A closed lipid boundary studded with proteins. It defines the cell and controls what crosses in and out.
The first complete cell: a membrane enclosing ribosomes, energy, and a loop of DNA. Simple, ancient, and alive.

items._bio_b3_note: Biology B3 multicellular components (Chem/Bio Biology track). eukaryotic_cell is CellPart; tissue/organ are Organism. Assembled by the Tissue Culture.
items.codex_entry: A cell with a nucleus and specialised organelles. Larger and more capable than its prokaryotic ancestors — the building block of complex life.
Many like cells acting as one. A sheet of coordinated eukaryotic cells performing a shared function.
Several tissues combined into a functional unit — a heart, a leaf, a liver. The machinery of a body.

items._bio_b4_note: Biology B4 whole-life tier (Chem/Bio Biology track). Category Organism. The Biology endgame, assembled by the Bioreactor.
items.codex_entry: Organs integrated into a single living whole that senses, moves, and reproduces. Chemistry has become a creature.
Many organisms of one kind, breeding and competing. Life at the scale where evolution takes hold.
Countless populations woven into one self-sustaining web — predators, prey, plants, and decomposers cycling matter and energy. A living world.

A ghostly particle with almost no mass. Trillions pass through you every second without touching a single atom. Fusion releases neutrinos that fly straight out of the reactor, carrying energy with them.
A high-energy packet of light. When two nuclei fuse, the new nucleus weighs slightly less than the pieces that made it; the missing mass leaves as a gamma ray (E = mc²).
Thorium-232 that has caught one neutron. It beta-decays within minutes into Protactinium-233, the first step of the thorium fuel cycle that breeds Uranium-233.
Radium-226 plus one neutron. A neutron inside it turns into a proton (beta decay), making Actinium-227.
A neutron-heavy radon that beta-decays into Francium-223, the only francium found in nature.
Radon stripped of eleven neutrons. Too proton-rich to last, it captures an electron and becomes Astatine-211, an isotope used in cancer therapy.
Lead-208 plus one neutron. It beta-decays into Bismuth-209, the heaviest element with a near-stable isotope.
Lead with seven neutrons removed. It captures an electron and becomes Thallium-201, used in heart scans.
CO: half-burnt carbon. With hydrogen it is syngas, the start of most organic chemistry.
H2O2: an oxidiser cells make and destroy every second.
CH2O: the simplest aldehyde. Five of them can join into a sugar.
CH3OH: wood alcohol, made from syngas.
HCOOH: the acid in ant stings, made from carbon monoxide and water.
HCN: deadly to us, yet five of them make adenine, a letter of the genetic code.
CO(NH2)2: the first organic molecule made from inorganic ones (Wohler, 1828).
C2H4: the simplest alkene, a plant hormone and the start of plastics.
C2H2: a triple-bonded fuel that burns hot enough to weld.
CH3COOH: vinegar, and the two-carbon unit cells build fats from.
C3H8O3: the three-carbon spine of every fat.
Sulfur as it occurs near volcanic vents. Life needs it for two amino acids.
H2S: rotten-egg gas from the vents, the sulfur source for cysteine.
Phosphorus reduced from phosphate rock: the backbone of DNA and the energy of ATP.
H3PO4: phosphate, the link in DNA's backbone and ATP's tail.
Glycerol with a phosphate: the head of a membrane lipid.
Rock salt, NaCl. Cells run on the difference between sodium outside and potassium inside.
Potassium chloride from evaporated seas.
Calcium carbonate. Shells, bones and the calcium signals in every cell.
The simplest amino acid.
A small amino acid, built from formaldehyde and ammonia.
An amino acid with an alcohol group.
The amino acid with sulfur: its bridges hold proteins in shape.
The five-carbon sugar in RNA and ATP.
A nucleobase made from five HCN: the A in DNA and the A in ATP.
A nucleobase: the G in the genetic code.
A nucleobase: the C in the genetic code.
A sixteen-carbon fatty acid, built two carbons at a time from acetic acid.
Two amino acids joined by a peptide bond: the start of every protein.
Adenosine monophosphate: adenine, ribose and one phosphate, a nucleotide.
A phosphate head and two fatty tails: it folds itself into membranes.
Adenosine triphosphate: the energy currency of every living cell.
Iron ore. Roasted, then reduced with carbon into steel.
Nearly pure carbon. Steel needs it; so does carbon fibre.
The ore of aluminium, a metal too reactive to find free.
The most common copper ore.
Titanium dioxide: strong, light titanium is locked inside.
Aluminium won by electrolysis: light, and it never rusts through.
Drawn copper, the conductor of every circuit.
A silicon wafer etched and wired with copper: the first machine part.

buildings.description: Extracts fundamental particles from quantum fields. Output depends on the field type it is placed on.
buildings._note_special_upgrade: Two adjacent harvesters on opposing polarity fields can be merged into a Nucleon Harvester.
buildings.tutorial_note: First building the player can place. Goes on the quark or lepton field. Unlocked by Automation I research.
buildings.codex_entry: Extracts fundamental particles from quantum fields. Place on a field to begin harvesting. Positive fields yield Up Quarks, negative fields yield Down Quarks, lepton fields yield Electrons.

buildings.description: Spans two quark fields and pulls whole protons or neutrons out of them, no Combiner needed. Place it from the Build menu, or merge two neighbouring Harvesters (one on Up Quarks, one on Down Quarks) from a Harvester's info panel.
buildings.tutorial_note: Not taught in the tutorial. Replaces two Harvesters plus a Strong Force Combiner.
buildings.codex_entry: Quarks are never found alone: they are always bound in groups of three. The Nucleon Harvester straddles two quark fields of opposite polarity and draws out whole protons (up, up, down) or neutrons (up, down, down), skipping the Combiner entirely.

buildings.description: Sorts a mixed belt. Items come in one side and leave by the side you choose for each item; anything you haven't assigned goes straight through.
buildings.tutorial_note: Not taught in the tutorial. Pure logistics: no recipe, no power, no craft time.
buildings.codex_entry: A sorting gate. Every item that arrives is checked against your rules and sent out of the matching side, so one belt can carry several items to several buildings.

buildings.description: Wells up clean water. Draw a channel from it and the stream carries whatever you drop in past every building on its banks. Its flow is shared by those buildings, upstream first.
buildings.tutorial_note: Chemistry streams: every channel starts at a Spring.
buildings.codex_entry: A spring is groundwater forced up through rock. Its flow sets how many reactors one stream can feed.

buildings.description: Sits at a stream's mouth and burns whatever reaches it, turning the energy stored in its bonds into entropy. Finished compounds pay far more than raw gas.
buildings.tutorial_note: Chemistry's sink. Without one, a stream's mouth sells leftovers at the surplus rate.
buildings.codex_entry: A bomb calorimeter measures the heat a substance releases when it burns: its enthalpy of combustion.

buildings.description: Fires neutrons at a heavy element until a proton breaks off, leaving the element one below it. Walks the metals down from Mercury to Cobalt.
buildings.codex_entry: Spallation: a fast particle chips nucleons off a heavy nucleus. Accelerators use it to make neutron beams; here it runs the table downhill, one element at a time.

buildings.description: Binds quarks into protons and neutrons using the strong nuclear force. Requires a power source within link range.
buildings.obsolete_condition: Nucleon Harvesting researched: a Nucleon Harvester makes protons and neutrons straight from quark fields.
buildings.tutorial_note: First powered building. Placement triggers the power system tutorial segment.
buildings.codex_entry: Uses the strong nuclear force to bind quarks into nucleons. Requires a power source within range to operate. Becomes obsolete once the Nucleon Harvester upgrade is unlocked.

buildings.description: Generates electron volts (eV) to power nearby buildings. Link multiple generators to share power across the grid.
buildings.tutorial_note: Introduced immediately after the Strong Force Combiner. Teaches power radius and the energy grid. Small radius (generates eV, short reach) — pair with the Power Relay to spread coverage.
buildings.codex_entry: Generates electron volts (eV) to power nearby buildings. Place within link range of powered buildings. Link multiple generators to share power across the grid.

buildings.description: Broadcasts the grid's shared power over a wide radius without generating any eV of its own. Place relays to carry power from your generators to distant buildings.
buildings._note_relay: A power SPREADER, not a source: is_power_source=true so PowerGridSystem treats its InfluenceRadius as a coverage box, but base_output_ev=0 means it adds nothing to the shared eV supply. link_radius_tiles is the connection range: the relay only extends coverage while it chains (link by link, within max of the two nodes' link ranges) back to a real generator. A relay not linked to any generator provides NO coverage (IsGridLinked=false) and is skipped entirely by PowerGridSystem.
buildings.codex_entry: A resonant broadcast mast. The Relay generates no power of its own — it re-radiates the grid's existing eV field across a far wider area than a generator can reach, letting a single power source feed buildings spread across the whole site.

buildings._comment: --- SPECIAL BUILDINGS (available from start, no research required) ---
buildings.description: Sorts raw particles from your inventory and converts their energy into base currency. The act of sorting increases local entropy — a price the Demon gladly pays.
buildings._note_entropy: EntropySinkTag is added by BuildingPlacer/BuildingAuthoring when is_entropy_sink=true. EntropySinkSystem handles conveyor-fed deposits (BuildingInputSlot). MaxwellsDemonController handles manual drag-and-drop deposits (InventorySlot). Both paths coexist.
buildings._note_demon_input: Maxwell's Demon is a pure entropy sink — no production output buffer. base_max_input_items_per_slot is 0 because it accepts all incoming items without limit (unlimited deposit queue).
buildings._note_demon_upgrades: output_rate here means throughput multiplier — how many items/second the Demon can process from conveyors. L2=2x, L3=4x base throughput.
buildings._note_demon_storage: Storage upgrades increase the Demon's internal pending-deposit queue size (items waiting to be processed for entropy).
buildings.tutorial_note: Pre-placed on the starting grid. Player deposits manually-collected particles here to earn the 100 base currency needed for Recombination I.
buildings.codex_entry: A thermodynamic thought experiment made real. Maxwell's Demon appears to violate the second law by sorting particles — but information erasure always costs energy. That cost manifests as entropy. The currency it generates is real. So is the entropy.

buildings.description: Assembles nucleons and electrons into atoms. Starts with hydrogen; research Nucleosynthesis to unlock heavier elements. Power cost scales with atomic mass.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (recipe-dynamic draw deferred). Legacy intent: atomic_mass × game_config.atomic_assembler_ev_per_mass_unit
buildings._note_ports: 2x1 since #275: Helium needs protons, neutrons and electrons on separate belts (a belt can't merge into another belt's head), and a 1x1 boxed in by its neighbours often had one usable side. Input.Facing = item travel direction, so the intake is on the OPPOSITE edge. Four intakes: the North edge of both cells (South-facing), the West end (East-facing) and the East end (West-facing). Output exits the South (front) edge of the left cell; the right cell's South edge is spare.
buildings.codex_entry: Combines protons, neutrons, and electrons into complete atoms. Power cost scales with the complexity of the element being assembled — heavier elements demand more energy.

buildings.description: Adds or removes neutrons: enriches Uranium into Uranium-235 and irradiates or strips the decay-chain elements. Slower than the Atom Generator by design.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (recipe-dynamic draw deferred). Legacy intent: neutrons_adjusted × game_config.isotopic_manipulator_ev_per_neutron
buildings.codex_entry: Adds or removes neutrons from a base element to produce isotopes. Radioactive isotopes produced here will emit decay particles over time if housed in a Radioactive Containment building.

buildings.description: Lets unstable isotopes decay: one isotope in, the element it becomes out, plus the particle it releases. Choose which output side each product leaves by.
buildings._note_footprint: Houses the Isotopic Manipulator inside it — larger footprint.
buildings._note_containment: Repurposed as the Decay Chamber (#322). Its two outputs carry the element and the released particle; the player assigns them per side (OutputPortFilter).
buildings.codex_entry: Required housing for any building producing radioactive isotopes. Safely contains decay events and harvests alpha and beta particles as usable energy currency.

buildings.description: Combines elements into molecules and simple compounds. The first step beyond atomic assembly.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (per-recipe draw deferred).
buildings.codex_entry: Drives covalent bond formation between elements at high energy density. Primary intake accepts the dominant element; secondary intake accepts the reactant. Output is one molecule unit per cycle.

buildings.description: Synthesises alloys and advanced materials from molecular precursors.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (per-recipe draw deferred).
buildings.codex_entry: Operates at extreme temperatures and pressures to force molecular precursors into stable alloy lattices. Slower than the Molecular Synthesizer by design — materials science demands patience.

buildings.description: Assembles advanced materials into high-precision megastructure components.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (per-recipe draw deferred).
buildings.codex_entry: The pinnacle of in-Foundry manufacturing. Operates at near-quantum precision, assembling materials into components that will eventually orbit a star. Each cycle takes minutes. Each output lasts millennia.

buildings.description: Fuses two light nuclei into a heavier element — the fast lane up the fusion ladder. Unlocked by Stellar Fusion research.
buildings._note_power: Static per-level eV draw. Nuclear reactors are high-draw consumers.
buildings._note_ports: Inputs on E/W/N edges, output on the S edge (mirrors the Atom Generator).
buildings.codex_entry: A magnetic-confinement chamber that forces light nuclei together against their mutual repulsion. Far faster than assembling heavy atoms nucleon-by-nucleon, but it only climbs as high as iron.

buildings.description: A breeder: Uranium soaks up the reactor's own neutrons and decays into Neptunium, then Plutonium.
buildings._note_power: Static per-level eV draw. Nuclear reactors are high-draw consumers.
buildings._note_ports: Inputs on E/W/N edges, output on the S edge (mirrors the Atom Generator).
buildings.codex_entry: A shielded rod-array core. A slow neutron splits a heavy fissile nucleus into two fragments closer to iron, releasing more neutrons to sustain the chain.

buildings.description: Draws raw feedstock from Chemistry's fields: hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen gas, graphite, and minerals.
buildings.codex_entry: A boring rig for matter itself. Placed on an element seam, it extracts a chosen element in bulk — the raw feedstock for chemistry.

buildings.description: Combines mined minerals with Chemistry's gases into salts and acids.
buildings.codex_entry: A reaction vessel that forces mined elements into bonds. Two intakes feed the reactants; one output delivers the compound.

buildings.description: Mines bulk metals from a Metal Lode. Place on a metal seam and pick which metal to extract.
buildings.codex_entry: A heavier cousin of the Element Harvester, geared for metal lodes. Extracts iron, copper, aluminum, or nickel to feed reactors and catalysts.

buildings.description: Drives industrial reactions: salts, strong acids, bases, and catalysts from mined elements and metals.
buildings.codex_entry: A pressurized vessel packed with catalytic surfaces. It forces reluctant reagents to react, turning mined stock into the salts, acids, and catalysts of heavy industry.

buildings.description: Assembles carbon chains and the biochemical precursors of life: hydrocarbons, alcohols, sugars, amino acids, fatty acids, and nucleotides.
buildings.codex_entry: A three-intake synthesis train for carbon chemistry. Hydrocarbons enter, and — once the biochemical precursors are understood — the four monomers of life emerge: sugar, amino acid, fatty acid, and nucleotide.

buildings.description: Harvests organic compounds from a living field. Place on an organic seam and pick which compound to extract.
buildings.codex_entry: A gentle extractor tuned for living matter. Placed on an organic seam, it draws out a chosen compound — glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, or nucleotides — the feedstock of the Biosynthesizer.

buildings.description: Assembles organic compounds into the four macromolecules of life: proteins, carbohydrates, lipid membranes, and nucleic acids.
buildings.codex_entry: A warm, enzyme-packed reactor that polymerises life's monomers. One intake of organic compound in; one macromolecule of life out.

buildings.description: Assembles biomolecules into organelles and whole prokaryotic cells.
buildings.codex_entry: A sterile assembly bay for cellular machinery. Biomolecules go in; ribosomes, organelles, and finally whole living cells come out.

buildings.description: Grows cells into nucleated eukaryotes, then into tissues and organs.
buildings.codex_entry: A perfused growth chamber. It nurtures cells into nucleated eukaryotes and coaxes them to bind into tissues and organs.

buildings.description: Integrates organs into whole organisms, then populations and entire ecosystems. The Biology endgame.
buildings.codex_entry: A world in a vessel. It grows organs into organisms, organisms into populations, and populations into a self-sustaining ecosystem — the summit of the Biology track.

fields._note_purchase: Bought from the Build menu after field_synthesis. Always placed as a pair (one Harvester per quark flavour). Price = base x multiplier^(pairs bought this run).
fields.codex_entry: A region of space dense with confined quarks. Positive-polarity zones yield Up Quarks; negative-polarity zones yield Down Quarks. Tap to extract a particle, then wait out the field's recharge.
A region saturated with free leptons. Tap to collect an Electron, then wait out the field's recharge. Electrons are essential for completing any atom.
A seam of naturally fissile ore. Tap or harvest to extract uranium — the cheapest on-ramp to matter heavier than iron, and the fuel for fission.
A bred-actinide deposit. Harvest plutonium — denser fission fuel, and the gateway to the transuranic ladder.
Free neutrons streaming out of the decaying ore around it. Harvest them to feed the Isotopic Manipulator, or strip them from heavy elements yourself.
Hydrogen gas bubbling up from below. Extract it for water, methane and ammonia.
A vent breathing out oxygen gas. Burn it with hydrogen to make water.
A seam of graphite, nearly pure carbon. Bought from the Build menu after Carbon Chemistry.
A vent of nitrogen gas. Bought from the Build menu after Nitrogen Fixation.
Calcium carbonate from old shells: calcium for bones and signals. Bought from the Build menu.
Potash: potassium chloride, the salt that keeps nerves firing. Bought from the Build menu.
Rock salt left by an ancient sea: sodium and chlorine for every cell. Bought from the Build menu.
Phosphorus locked in rock, reduced to red phosphorus as it is extracted. Bought from the Build menu.
Yellow crusts of native sulfur around a fumarole. Bought from the Build menu.

fields._organic_fields_note: Biology (Chem/Bio Biology track) feedstock. field_type 'Organic' (shared) so one Organic Harvester works on all four. They drop the OrganicCompound items (mined, not synthesized) — the same items Chemistry C4 also crafts. Introduced per-site via the absolute-count density-override path on site_bio_lab.
fields.codex_entry: A field thick with photosynthetic bloom, dense in sugars. Harvest glucose — the universal cellular fuel and the base of every carbohydrate.
A primordial pool rich in free amino acids. Harvest them to feed the assembly of proteins.
An oily seep of long-chain fatty acids. Harvest them to build the membranes that give cells their boundary.
A vein laced with free nucleotides. Harvest them to spell out nucleic acids — the memory of life.
ATP welling up from a vent of living chemistry: energy, ready to spend.
Red iron ore, Fe2O3, the ore most of the world's iron comes from.
Carbon laid down by ancient forests: the fuel and the carbon in steel.
Silica sand, SiO2: glass, wafers and aerogel start here.
Aluminium ore, smelted by electrolysis.
Copper iron sulfide: brassy gold, and the copper in every wire.
Titanium dioxide crystals, reduced to titanium by the Kroll process.

_managers_note: Hireable building managers (Idle Planet Miner-style crew). Each grants ONE passive bonus to ONE assigned building. bonus_type: CraftSpeed (multiplies ProductionSpeed), OutputQuantity (multiplies recipe output, floor), PowerDiscount (reduces eV draw; bonus_value is the multiplier kept, e.g. 0.8 = -20%). hire_cost_prestige is in prestige currency. Hired managers + assignments survive prestige.

lines.text: Welcome. I am The Architect — your guide through the Quantum Foundry. This facility builds matter from scratch, starting with the smallest particles in existence.
Everything solid in the universe — planets, stars, you — began as fundamental particles. Your job is to harvest them, combine them, and build upward.
See that glowing blue field? That is a Lepton Field — saturated with free electrons. Every atom you will ever build needs them.
Tap it. Pull electrons into your inventory.
Good work. Those electrons gave you your first entropy — the currency that powers this facility. But entropy alone cannot build matter.
That orange field is a Quark Field. It generates Up Quarks and Down Quarks in equal measure every time you mine it — the raw ingredients for every proton and neutron you will ever craft.
Excellent work. You've synthesized protons and neutrons and converted them to entropy — the fundamental energy of this facility.
The field glows where particles accumulate. Tap it to pull electrons into your inventory.
Maxwell's Demon extracts entropy from the energy difference between sorted particles. Deposit what you have collected.
Drag the electrons to the deposit side. The Demon converts particle energy into entropy — the base currency of this facility.
Good. Those electrons built your first entropy. It is a small number for now.
Quarks are raw particles, like your electrons - the Demon values them the same for now. The real yield comes from organizing them. Bring them in.
Deposit all of them. Raw matter yields little on its own - but bind these quarks into protons and atoms, and the Demon pays far more. That is the path ahead.
You have enough to begin. Open the menu on the left — the Research panel is there.
The research tree is your progression map. Each node unlocks new processes, new materials, new machinery. Nothing in this facility advances without it.
Recombination I. This unlocks the strong nuclear force — the force that binds quarks into nucleons. Purchase it.
Recombination I is active. The strong nuclear force is now at your disposal — the most powerful fundamental force in nature, and the one that makes atomic structure possible.

A proton is two Up Quarks and one Down Quark — net charge +1, the core of every hydrogen atom. A neutron is one Up Quark and two Down Quarks — net charge zero, the stabilizing mass inside every nucleus beyond hydrogen.
The recipe panel holds every synthesis process you have unlocked. Open it and find the proton recipe.
Two Up Quarks, one Down Quark, bound by the strong force. The result: a proton. Charge +1. The nucleus of the simplest atom in existence. Craft two.
Now the neutron — one Up Quark, two Down Quarks. Net charge zero, but nearly identical mass to the proton. Inside a nucleus, neutrons neutralize the repulsion between protons. Craft two.
Protons and neutrons carry significantly more energy than raw quarks. The Demon values organized matter — each layer of complexity compounds your entropy yield. Bring them in.
Deposit both the protons and the neutrons. You have built the first organized matter this facility has produced.
Complexity yields more entropy. That principle will drive every decision as this facility scales.
Hydrogen synthesis is unlocked. To build a hydrogen atom you need a proton — which you now know how to build — and one electron from the Lepton Field.
Gather your materials: 4 Up Quarks and 2 Down Quarks to build two protons, plus 2 electrons to complete the atoms.
Build the protons first. Two Up Quarks, one Down Quark each. Two protons means two hydrogen atoms.
The final step: combine a proton and an electron. The electromagnetic attraction between the positive nucleus and the negative lepton creates a stable atomic orbital. Craft your hydrogen.
Hydrogen. Atomic number 1. The most abundant element in the observable universe — and you built two of them from quarks and energy alone.
Hydrogen atoms carry more bound energy than raw particles. Organized matter always yields more entropy — the Demon knows the difference. Bring it in.
You have enough entropy to unlock Automation I — your first engineering breakthrough. It enables the Harvester: a field collector that gathers particles on a continuous cycle, no tapping required.
This is the transition point. Manual harvesting was a lesson. The Harvester is how you scale.
Open the Research panel and purchase Automation I.
Automation I. Purchase it — then you can place your first Harvester.

The Harvester collects into its output buffer. A conveyor carries those particles to Maxwell's Demon automatically. Open the conveyor tool, then tap the tile beside the Harvester's output to set the start. Tap the tile in front of the Demon's input and I will route the belt for you. Tap the check to place it, then Done when you are finished.
Open the Build menu and place a Harvester on the lepton field. It will collect electrons automatically - you will need a steady supply of them for hydrogen later.
Your factory is running. Buildings produce at their rated output continuously — no manual input required.
It keeps working while you are away, too. Close the game and your automated buildings still earn entropy at 20% of their normal rate, for up to 2 hours. You will be able to raise both limits later.

As production scales, entropy accumulates. But there is a ceiling on each run. When your net worth approaches the prestige threshold, you will have extracted most of this run's value — and it will be time to reset.
You have reached the ceiling. Prestige is not failure — it is the mechanism that converts one-time progress into permanent power.
The reset clears your inventory, buildings, and entropy. What you keep: prestige currency, to spend on permanent upgrades that speed up every run. Initiate it — you will return faster than you left.
The reset is complete. The facility rebuilds, but you are not starting over — you are starting ahead.
You carry prestige currency now. Unlike entropy, it does not reset between runs. Spend it on permanent upgrades that will accelerate every future run.
Open the upgrade shop. Each purchase compounds across every future run. Spend wisely.
Your quark Harvesters are running. You already have Recombination I — the Strong Force Combiner fuses quarks into protons. Keep accumulating entropy and we will put those quarks to work.
Place the Strong Force Combiner anywhere on the grid. It will show as unpowered until you connect a generator — we will handle that next.
The Generator produces electron volts — a local power field. Any powered building within its radius draws from it automatically. Place one near the Combiner.

No wiring needed — the Combiner is already inside the Generator's power field, so it comes online the moment a generator is in range. It draws 10 eV, well within the Generator's 50 eV output. Watch the power readout up top: if total draw ever exceeds supply, everything slows down.

Electrons are only part of the story. Place a Harvester on each quark field. A quark field holds both Up and Down Quarks, so when you place each Harvester, choose what it collects: one for Up Quarks, one for Down Quarks.
Connect your quark Harvesters to the Combiner with conveyors: tap the tile beside a Harvester's output, then the tile in front of the Combiner's input. Quarks will flow in continuously.
Open the Combiner and set its recipe to Proton - two Up Quarks and one Down Quark each. A proton is the nucleus of hydrogen, so protons are what we want flowing next.
Run a conveyor from the Combiner's proton output to Maxwell's Demon. Protons sell for 3 entropy each - triple what a raw quark brings.
Protons selling automatically alongside your electrons. The quark Harvester feeds the Combiner, the Combiner feeds the Demon - income with no tapping required.
The Atom Generator is available — you researched it when you unlocked Hydrogen Synthesis. Save up 350 entropy and place it.
Nucleons are selling. But a proton and an electron together can become something more. The Atom Generator takes one of each and produces hydrogen — your first complete atom. It is ready to place.

Place the Atom Generator on the glowing tiles. It draws 20 eV, and a generator only powers buildings inside its influence circle, so the glow marks a spot in range of your Basic Generator. It is two tiles wide with four intakes, and the glow leaves room for a belt at each one: hydrogen needs protons and electrons now, and helium will need neutrons too.
Re-route the proton belt from the Combiner to the Atom Generator's proton input, then route your electron Harvester into its electron input. Protons plus electrons become hydrogen.

Connect the Atom Generator's output to Maxwell's Demon. Hydrogen sells for 5 entropy. A raw proton and electron would have sold for 4 — assembly adds one entropy per cycle, and that margin compounds as you scale.
Hydrogen. One proton, one electron — the simplest atom in existence, and the most abundant in the universe. Your factory is making it continuously, without your input.
Every element above hydrogen needs neutrons as well as protons. Before you build for them, teach the Atom Generator what to do with them.
Field Synthesis costs two hundred and fifty entropy. It lets you place new quark and lepton fields wherever there is empty space.
The vacuum will give. Quark fields always form in pairs, one for each flavour you harvest. Open the Build menu and place a Quark Field Pair on two empty tiles.
Choose the spot well. Every field you place costs ten times the one before it.
A second pair. Put a Harvester on each, Up and Down, and feed them into a second Strong Force Combiner set to Neutron.
Protons from one Combiner, neutrons from the other, electrons from your lepton field. That is everything helium needs, and your Atom Generator already knows what to do with it.
Before you start saving — your factory is running at base efficiency. Every building here can be upgraded on two separate tracks: Speed and Storage.
Speed upgrades multiply throughput. Level 2 doubles your production rate. Level 4 brings you to eight times the base. Same inputs, same power draw — delivered faster.
Storage upgrades expand the output buffer — how many items a building holds before it stalls. A larger buffer means the factory keeps running longer while you are away.
Tap the Atom Generator. We are upgrading its speed first — it is the bottleneck of your hydrogen line.

dialogues._worlds_intro_note: Chem/Bio Phase 5: one-shot intro dialogue played the first time each World is unlocked from the Worlds panel (WorldsSubController). Dialogue id convention is 'intro_' + world id.

lines.text: You have crossed a threshold. Physics forged the elements one nucleus at a time. Out here they come as nature leaves them: hydrogen and oxygen as gases, carbon as graphite, nitrogen in the air.
Chemistry is open. Travel there from the Worlds panel whenever you wish; every world keeps producing while you are away. I will show you how things work when you arrive.
Hydrogen and oxygen seep up from the ground as gas. Place a Hydrogen Seep on the glowing tile just below the stream, then an Oxygen Vent on the tile beside it.
Now draw a Channel from the tile below the Spring straight to the Calorimeter's side. That is your stream: it carries whatever is dropped into it down to the Calorimeter.
Remember this: the stream runs past buildings, in front of them, never into them. Everything you build goes beside the water.
One more rule: a Spring's flow is limited, and buildings share it nearest the source first. The bar at the top shows how much is used.
When the last buildings run short of water, add another Spring and start a new stream. The lab is yours.
Water is flowing to the Calorimeter. It burns whatever reaches it for entropy; finished compounds pay far more than raw gas. Tap it any time to burn what you carry, just like the Demon.

Now a reaction. Place a Molecular Synthesizer on the glowing tile below the stream, downstream of the vents. Its arrows face the water too: it takes what its recipe needs as the stream passes, lets everything else float on, and drops what it makes back in.
An Extractor on each vent draws the gas out and drops it into the water in front of it. Its arrow must point up at the stream; that is the side it drops into.
First, water. A Spring wells it up. Place one on the glowing tile, up and to the left of the Calorimeter.
Welcome to the lab. Chemistry plays by different rules: there is no power here, and no Maxwell's Demon. Water does the work, and the Calorimeter in the middle turns finished chemicals into entropy.
Every reaction is an equation. Two hydrogen and one oxygen make two water. I have set aside enough entropy for your first stream; spend it on the Chemistry Lab first.
From dead chemistry, something new: matter that copies itself. Biology takes the organic precursors you have learned to make and assembles them into the machinery of life.
Harvest organic compounds from the living fields, build biomolecules, then cells, tissues, organs — and at last a whole ecosystem. This is the summit of the journey: from quarks to a living world.
Life is complete, and it needs tools. Deep in the crust the elements you forged lie as ores: iron in hematite, copper in chalcopyrite, aluminium in bauxite, titanium in rutile.
Metallurgy is open. Travel there from the Worlds panel. Smelt ores into steel and alloys, and the alloys into the materials a megastructure needs.
Welcome to the foundry. Here ores are mined, not made, and Maxwell's Demon is back to turn what you smelt into entropy.
I have set aside enough entropy to open your first seam. Study Ore Prospecting first.
Hematite, red iron ore. Place a seam anywhere on the map.
A Metal Harvester on the seam digs the ore out. Point its output at the Demon.
Ore reaches the Demon. Next, Roasting opens the Materials Forge: two hematite make iron oxide, and iron oxide with coal makes steel.
Physics, chemistry, life and metal: you have every material. Engineering puts them together into machines, and the machines into a megastructure around the star.
Engineering is open. Its parts take materials from every world; carry them in your inventory and the Component Fabricator draws on it.
The assembly bay. Nothing grows or is mined here: every part is built from what the other worlds make.
I have set aside enough entropy for Circuitry. A circuit board is a wafer and copper wire from Metallurgy.
Place a Component Fabricator. It takes its parts from your inventory when nothing feeds it by belt.
Each Engineering part is slow and precious. The last is the Dyson Node; finish every research in one run and you can Ascend from the Megastructure panel.
Two times throughput. The Atom Generator now produces hydrogen at twice the rate for the same input cost. Your entropy income just doubled.
The Storage track works the same way — tap the building again and you will see it below the Speed upgrade. A larger output buffer means the line keeps running while you are offline.
Both tracks reset on prestige. The entropy you invest here comes back as a discount on your next run — every upgrade makes the next cycle faster.
Your factory runs on its own. Hydrogen flows from quark to atom to entropy — that is the foundation. Everything that follows builds on this loop.
The Research panel shows your next frontier. Nucleosynthesis opens the rest of the periodic table — but it costs five hundred entropy. Let the factory accumulate it.

Nucleosynthesis. Every element above hydrogen follows the same principle: proton count defines the element, neutron count defines its isotope. The Atom Generator supports all of them once this is purchased.

Nucleosynthesis is active. Helium-4 is now craftable — two protons, two neutrons, two electrons. It sells for ten entropy, twice hydrogen, so on its own it earns no more. Its real value is as fuel for something far bigger.
Helium-4 is as far as the Atom Generator goes. Every heavier element must be fused from lighter ones, and that road starts with Helium.

Helium-4 is as far as the Atom Generator goes. You have protons and electrons. Neutrons are what is missing, and both of your quark fields already feed the Combiner. Research Field Synthesis to condense new fields of your own.
Helium-4. The second element. Formed in the first three minutes after the Big Bang through primordial nucleosynthesis — you have just replicated one of the universe's oldest reactions.
Building it one nucleon at a time is slow, and the Atom Generator will go no further than this. Heavier atoms must be fused. I have sent you 6,500 entropy toward that road.
Heavy Elements research teaches the Atom Generator to build Uranium: 92 protons, 146 neutrons, 92 electrons. Atomic mass 238. One atom takes nearly four minutes and sells for 64 entropy.
Uranium is not worth building for its own sake. It is where the decay chain begins: Radioactive Isotopes lets it decay step by step down to Lead, and every step is worth more than the last.
Heavy Elements research acquired. Set an Atom Generator to Uranium. Later, Fissile Extraction opens Uranium fields on the Actinide Vein, a far cheaper source.
Uranium. Stars cannot forge anything heavier than iron without spending more energy than they gain. What you just built takes a supernova, or two neutron stars colliding.
It is also unstable. Radioactive Isotopes lets it decay toward Lead, and lets you enrich it into Uranium-235, the fuel for fission.

Uranium-235 is the fissile isotope. Enrichment removes three neutrons from Uranium-238, shifting it from nearly stable to critically unstable. The process releases an alpha particle — a helium-4 nucleus ejected from the atom.

Before producing radioactive isotopes, you need a Radioactive Containment structure. It houses the Manipulator, absorbs decay events, and converts emitted particles into usable energy. Place it first.

Radioactive Isotopes research complete. The Radioactive Containment building is now available. Place it before operating the Manipulator for fissile materials — without it, decay products are uncontrolled.

The Containment structure occupies a 2×2 footprint and draws 30 eV. Place an Isotopic Manipulator inside it to handle radioactive synthesis. Alpha and Beta particles from decay are collected automatically and returned to your power grid.
Uranium-235. Enriched nuclear fuel, worth many times ordinary Uranium, and enrichment releases three spare neutrons you can put to work elsewhere.
Split it in a Fission Reactor and it becomes two lighter elements worth several times the fuel, plus neutrons for capture. The alpha particles your Decay Chamber releases sell at Maxwell's Demon.
Alpha and Beta particles are the debris of nuclear instability. What is a hazard anywhere else is a resource here: sell them at Maxwell's Demon.

You have built matter from nothing — quarks to nucleons, nucleons to atoms, atoms to isotopes, isotopes to fissile fuel. This is the current frontier of the Quantum Foundry. The next tier of synthesis is ahead. Keep building.
Stars do not build helium from loose particles. They start with deuterium: one proton and one neutron, already bound together. Hydrogen's heavy twin.
Research Deuterium Synthesis and your Atom Generator can make it from a proton, a neutron and an electron, quicker than helium.
Two deuterium nuclei, pressed together hard enough, fuse into helium. That is a Fusion Reactor's whole job: join light nuclei into heavier ones, climbing the ladder toward iron.

Every fusion turns a sliver of mass into energy. It leaves the reactor as particles — gamma rays, neutrinos — that pass straight through your walls. Each one that escapes is paid out as bonus entropy.
Feed the reactor Deuterium and it makes Helium. A second reactor fed that Helium makes Carbon: three Helium-4 for one Carbon, worth 160 entropy.
Matter heavier than iron cannot be cheaply fused into being — it must be mined. Fissile Extraction opens uranium and plutonium veins: the raw fuel for the other half of the nuclear ladder.
Fusion climbs up to iron; fission breaks back down to it. You now command both directions of the nuclear ladder. Build, balance, and bank the entropy — the Foundry is yours.

dialogues._comment: Last tutorial line (#275): names the goals that left the tutorial. 2026-11-19: also introduces the Chemistry task list and the Cyclotron; 2026-11-24: belt path splitting tip.

lines.text: Carbon. The backbone of every living thing, and you forged it from quarks. Your factory now earns several times what hydrogen ever did.
From here the Foundry is yours. The Research panel climbs on through the light elements to Silicon. Past that, the heavier elements and every molecule wait for Chemistry.

To open Chemistry, work through the task list that appears at the top of the screen. Each stage asks for elements: send them to Maxwell's Demon and they count toward it while still paying entropy. Progress carries over when you prestige, so it takes a few runs. Tap the list to see what the current stage needs.
A tip for your belts: hold any belt to split it, sending its items two or three ways. The (i) on the Conveyor Belt card in the Build menu has the details.

One more tool is coming. After your second prestige the Cyclotron opens in the menu: kick a particle around its ring for 30 seconds and everything your factory earns is multiplied, up to three times, for a few minutes. It recharges, so come back to it. Build, balance, and bank the entropy.
